## Overview

Fixes #60262 by skipping FlashInfer attention during auto-selection when neither its JIT cache nor runtime build path is usable. This lets the selector fall back to `TRITON_ATTN` without changing `has_flashinfer()` semantics.

## Claims

- Add an attention-specific JIT availability check; `flashinfer-cubin` alone does not make FlashInfer attention JIT modules available.
- Skip FlashInfer during configuration validation unless `has_flashinfer()` is true and either `nvcc` + `ninja` are available or a JIT-cache provider advertises non-empty module and architecture metadata compatible with the active GPU.
- Cover the shim-without-provider, provider-without-cubins-or-compiler, matching-provider, architecture compatibility, and SM120/FP8 auto-selection fallback cases with CPU-only tests.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py -q` - 24 passed on Mac at head `a96250c` (reported by Denel; not independently rerun here).
- No GPU end-to-end serving or model evaluation was run for this revision. The added tests mock device/package/toolchain inputs and check selection and provider metadata; they do not load every attention-kernel artifact on hardware. The issue's RTX 5090 Badgr command was not run.

## Details

The issue reports that auto-selection chooses FlashInfer when the required attention JIT path is not usable. The attention-specific predicate first requires `has_flashinfer()`. It then accepts runtime compilation when both `nvcc` and `ninja` are available, or a JIT-cache provider with non-empty module and architecture metadata that matches FlashInfer 0.7.2's CUDA SASS target compatibility rule: `a` targets require the same major and minor; `f` and unsuffixed targets accept the same major with an equal or higher device minor. If the active device architecture cannot be read, the check uses the provider metadata fallback and cannot confirm compatibility with that GPU. Metadata presence also does not guarantee that every specific kernel artifact loads. The check remains separate from `has_flashinfer()` and its other callers.

Thanks @nej1gotnochill for the discussion on keeping this check attention-specific and leaving `has_flashinfer()` unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: no equivalent open PR found via gh searches run from my Mac.

AI assistance (Cursor) contributed to this change. I reviewed the patch and ran the tests listed above.

Added the parametrized case for both predicate states: usable -> FLASHINFER, unusable -> TRITON_ATTN. It's a selector unit test with the predicate mocked, so it doesn't import or run FlashInfer. On the artifact question: is_flashinfer_jit_usable only checks package and toolchain prerequisites. It doesn't verify per-kernel artifacts for the active architecture, and the docstring now says that explicitly. A real per-architecture artifact check would mean running the kernels, which is out of scope for this guard. Does the documented limitation cover it, or do you want the runtime check??

I ran this end to end on a **Tesla T4 (SM75)**, since that's where this crash
will hit most often once #55380 makes FlashInfer selectable on Turing again.
On Turing, FlashAttention isn't available, so FlashInfer becomes the first
candidate.

**Setup:** g4dn.2xlarge, main @ 242e4213f + this PR + #55380's SM75 floor
change, pip install (flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1, no flashinfer-cubin), ninja
on PATH, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B fp16, fresh `~/.cache/flashinfer` for each case.

| case | `is_flashinfer_jit_usable()` | selected | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| no nvcc, no jit-cache | False | TRITON_ATTN | ✅ runs |
| nvcc, no jit-cache | True | FLASHINFER | ✅ runs |
| **flashinfer-jit-cache 0.7.0.post1+cu130, no nvcc** | **True** | **FLASHINFER** | ❌ `RuntimeError: Could not find nvcc and default cuda_home='/usr/local/cuda' doesn't exist` |
| jit-cache + nvcc | True | FLASHINFER | ✅ runs |

For reference, without this PR the first case crashes with the same "Could
not find nvcc" error. So this PR fixes the plain pip install on T4.
`tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py`: 8 passed on the T4.

**The third row is a gap on SM75.** The `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel doesn't
include SM75 kernels (#55380 adds a warning about this), so on Turing
FlashInfer still JIT-compiles even when the cache is installed, and still
needs nvcc. A possible tweak:

```diff
-    if importlib.util.find_spec("flashinfer_jit_cache") is not None:
+    # flashinfer-jit-cache ships no SM75 kernels, so SM75 always needs the JIT.
+    if importlib.util.find_spec(
+        "flashinfer_jit_cache"
+    ) is not None and not current_platform.is_device_capability(75):
         return True
```

With that applied on the same T4, the third case selects TRITON_ATTN and runs,
and the jit-cache + nvcc case still selects FLASHINFER and runs. One of the new
cases in `test_flashinfer_utils.py` (jit-cache installed means usable) then
fails on an SM75 machine, so it would need the capability mocked.

Only SM75 matters here, and only after #55380, so it could also be left to
that PR. I'm happy to rerun anything on the T4.

_AI assistance (Claude) was used to run these tests and draft this comment. I
reviewed the setup and the results._

@emp7i thanks for running this on a T4 and catching the jit-cache edge. I added the SM75 guard in is_flashinfer_jit_usable() and updated the test to mock the device capability, covering both non-SM75 and SM75 with the cache installed. The focused suite passes here. I haven't rerun the end-to-end case on a T4 with this patch, so I can't claim that hardware verification. If you're still up for it, a rerun of the jit-cache case on your T4 against the updated branch would close the loop.

@denelbjohn18 I reran this on the T4 against b18f73337, using the same setup as before (main @ 242e4213f + this PR + #55380's SM75 floor change, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B fp16, fresh `~/.cache/flashinfer` for each case), with `flashinfer-jit-cache 0.7.0.post1+cu130` installed:

|---|---|---|---|
| jit-cache, no nvcc | False | TRITON_ATTN | ✅ runs (was ❌ "Could not find nvcc") |

_AI assistance (Claude) was used to run these tests and draft this comment. I reviewed the setup and the results._

Reading this against main `153a17166e` and FlashInfer 0.7.2, the jit-cache branch looks too loose.
Setup: this head `b18f73337b`, FlashInfer 0.7.2 with `flashinfer-jit-cache` 0.7.2+cu130 and its `sm120f` provider; source reading plus CPU probes, no GPU run.

1. **The shim alone passes.** In 0.7.2 `flashinfer-jit-cache` is a shim and the kernels come from per-arch provider packages, so `find_spec("flashinfer_jit_cache")` also passes when no provider is installed (`get_jit_cache_providers()` returns nothing).
2. **A provider alone is not enough either.** With a provider but no flashinfer-cubin or usable nvcc, and `VLLM_HAS_FLASHINFER_CUBIN=0`, `has_flashinfer()` is still False, so calling `flashinfer_xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` reaches `_missing`.

**Suggested gate:** `has_flashinfer() and ((nvcc and ninja) or compatible_provider)`. A CPU probe of the selector then chooses:

| Installed (no nvcc) | `has_flashinfer()` | Selected backend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| jit-cache shim, no provider | False | TRITON_ATTN |
| jit-cache shim plus the `sm120f` provider | False | TRITON_ATTN |
| flashinfer-cubin plus the provider | True | FLASHINFER |

The probe runs the real selector and availability functions, with package availability, backend order and other capability checks mocked.

**Why not widen `has_flashinfer()` instead:** that would also enable `concat_mla_k` for qualifying MLA dimensions, and the sm120f provider lacks its `concat_mla` module.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= python3 -I provider_probe.py shim   # providers=0
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= python3 -I provider_probe.py full   # provider=sm120f; modules=566; concat_mla_in_manifest=False
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= python3 -I selector_probe.py <vllm main tree>
```

```
shim: has_flashinfer=False; original_PR=True; proposed=False; selector=TRITON_ATTN; XQA=_missing
provider: has_flashinfer=False; original_PR=True; proposed=False; selector=TRITON_ATTN; XQA=_missing
kernels: has_flashinfer=True; original_PR=True; proposed=True; selector=FLASHINFER; XQA=mock_xqa
```
</details>

The probes, their output and a README with the package setup are in https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/e352c330e937596cf3da27fd06aceeb1.

@waynehacking8 Thanks for catching this. I agree that the jit-cache shim can be present without any kernel provider, and that a provider alone is not enough when `has_flashinfer()` is false. I kept `has_flashinfer()` as the first check, then made the attention path require either nvcc plus ninja or a jit-cache provider with non-empty module and architecture metadata. When the active device architecture is available, the provider architecture must match it. If it cannot be read, the check falls back to non-empty provider metadata, so it cannot confirm the provider targets the active device. The exact architecture-name match may also reject compatible suffixed targets.

I added CPU cases for the shim without a provider, a provider without cubins or a usable compiler, cubins with a matching provider, and the metadata fallback. I ran the focused tests on my Mac with VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu and 13 passed. This checks provider metadata, not whether every specific kernel artifact loads.

@denelbjohn18 Thanks, the provider check is the right shape. The exact name match does reject the stock provider, though: FlashInfer 0.7.2's `flashinfer-jit-cache-sm120f` advertises `sm120f`, so on SM120 and SM121 it never equals the `sm120` or `sm121` the new check builds.

**CPU selector probe** (real 0.7.2 cubin, jit-cache shim and `sm120f` provider; no nvcc or ninja; FP8 KV; device capability mocked; this head's diff applied to main `a9bf45ed8a`):

| Device | main | this head | this head with FlashInfer's rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SM120 | FLASHINFER | TRITON_ATTN | FLASHINFER |
| SM121 | FLASHINFER | TRITON_ATTN | FLASHINFER |

So a `vllm download-kernels` install on a machine without nvcc moves from FlashInfer to Triton, which is the case the provider branch is meant to accept.

**Suggestion:** reuse FlashInfer's own rule, `select_compatible_cuda_architecture()` in `flashinfer/jit/_cuda_architecture.py` (0.7.2), or mirror it: an `a` target needs the same major and minor, while `f` and unsuffixed targets run on the same major with an equal or higher minor. FlashInfer accepts `sm120a` on SM120 as well, so the `sm120a` case at `tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py` L108-L119 would flip to accepted.

The probe, its output and the setup are in https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/0699386705fbb97ea21c5db886d2ac2b. This checks selection only; I did not run attention on a GPU.

@waynehacking8 Thanks for the probe and the gist. That exposed a real regression. I replaced the exact name match with a mirror of FlashInfer 0.7.2's compatibility rule: an `a` target needs the same major and minor, while an `f` or unsuffixed target is accepted on the same major when its minor is no newer than the device. That accepts `sm120f` on SM120 and SM121, and `sm120a` on SM120 but not SM121. I updated the SM120 `sm120a` test case accordingly. I compared the mirror against the tagged 0.7.2 source logic over 84 provider and device pairs and found no differences. On my Mac, the focused CPU tests passed: 24 passed with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. If the device architecture cannot be read, the current check falls back to non-empty provider metadata, which cannot confirm a match to the active device. Provider metadata also does not prove that every specific attention kernel artifact will load.

Rechecked a96250c273 with the same CPU selector probe: with the stock `sm120f` provider and no nvcc, SM120 and SM121 FP8 KV selection is FLASHINFER again, the same as main. Your rule also agrees with FlashInfer 0.7.2's `select_compatible_cuda_architecture()` on all 432 pairs I tried (36 provider targets against 12 unsuffixed devices), and `tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py` passes here (24 passed). The output and scripts are in the same gist, https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/0699386705fbb97ea21c5db886d2ac2b (`README-a96250c273.md`); this checks selection and unit tests only, not attention on a GPU.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

One edge case worth clarifying is that this treats the presence of flashinfer_jit_cache as sufficient for the attention JIT usability, Does that guarantee the required attention kernel is available for the active architecture particularly SM120 or can the cache be installed without a matching artifact? If the package guarantees the needed coverage then documenting that assumption would help otherwise could we add a check or test for this case? Otherwise the attention specific availability check looks like a good approach for this issue...

+):
+    """Select Triton on SM120 if unavailable; preserve FlashInfer otherwise.
+
+    The lightweight backend stub models the proposed attention-specific
+    predicate. This keeps the test independent of FlashInfer's optional
+    runtime package and does not change the broader ``has_flashinfer()`` check.

+    except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
+        if error.name != "vllm._C_stable_libtorch":
+            raise
+        # CUDA platform import normally imports this extension to register ops.
+        # Selector-only coverage does not call those ops, so stand in for the
+        # extension when testing from an unbuilt source checkout.
+        sys.modules["vllm._C_stable_libtorch"] = ModuleType("vllm._C_stable_libtorch")
+
+    from vllm.platforms.cuda import CudaPlatform
+    from vllm.utils import flashinfer as flashinfer_utils

+        @classmethod

+            return (__name__, "FlashInferBackendStub")

+            return "FLASHINFER"
+
+        @classmethod
+        def is_attention_jit_usable(cls):

+def _is_compatible_flashinfer_cuda_architecture(
+    provider_architecture: str, device_architecture: str
+) -> bool:
+    """Mirror FlashInfer 0.7.2 SASS target compatibility for provider metadata."""
+    pattern = r"sm(?P<major>[0-9]{1,2})(?P<minor>[0-9])(?P<suffix>[af]?)"
+    provider = re.fullmatch(pattern, provider_architecture)
+    device = re.fullmatch(pattern, device_architecture)
+    if provider is None or device is None:
+        return False
+
+    provider_major = int(provider.group("major"))
+    provider_minor = int(provider.group("minor"))
+    device_major = int(device.group("major"))
+    device_minor = int(device.group("minor"))
+    suffix = provider.group("suffix")
+
+    if suffix == "a":
+        return (provider_major, provider_minor) == (device_major, device_minor)
+    return provider_major == device_major and provider_minor <= device_minor
+
+
+def _has_compatible_flashinfer_jit_cache_provider() -> bool:
+    """Return whether an installed provider advertises kernels for this GPU."""
+    if importlib.util.find_spec("flashinfer_jit_cache") is None:
+        return False
+    try:
+        providers = importlib.import_module(
+            "flashinfer_jit_cache"
+        ).get_jit_cache_providers()
+    except (AttributeError, ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError, RuntimeError, ValueError):
+        return False
+
+    providers = tuple(providers)
+    if not providers:
+        return False
+
+    try:
+        device_capability = current_platform.get_device_capability()
+    except (NotImplementedError, RuntimeError):
+        device_capability = None
+    if device_capability is None:
+        # Some platforms cannot expose a capability before device setup. Require
+        # the provider to advertise both modules and architectures, but note
+        # that this cannot establish a match to the active device.
+        return any(
+            provider.modules and provider.cuda_architectures for provider in providers
+        )
+
+    device_architecture = f"sm{device_capability.to_int()}"
+    return any(
+        _is_compatible_flashinfer_cuda_architecture(architecture, device_architecture)
+        for provider in providers
+        if provider.modules and provider.cuda_architectures
+        for architecture in provider.cuda_architectures
+    )
+

+def is_flashinfer_jit_usable() -> bool:
+    """Check whether FlashInfer attention JIT has a usable build or AOT path.
+
+    FlashInfer's runtime JIT needs both nvcc and ninja. The jit-cache shim
+    alone does not provide kernels; a provider must advertise at least one
+    module for the active GPU architecture. The separate cubin package only
+    supplies TRTLLM-gen cubins and is not sufficient for attention JIT modules.
+    This check does not verify per-kernel artifacts; it decides eligibility,
+    not whether every specific kernel can load.
+    """
+    if not has_flashinfer():
+        return False
+
+    if _flashinfer_nvcc_path() is not None and shutil.which("ninja") is not None:
+        return True
+
+    # flashinfer-jit-cache ships no SM75 kernels, so SM75 needs the JIT.
+    if current_platform.is_device_capability(75):
+        return False
+
+    return _has_compatible_flashinfer_jit_cache_provider()

Added the parametrized case for both predicate states: usable -> FLASHINFER, unusable -> TRITON_ATTN. It's a selector unit test with the predicate mocked, so it doesn't import or run FlashInfer. On the artifact question: is_flashinfer_jit_usable only checks package and toolchain prerequisites. It doesn't verify per-kernel artifacts for the active architecture, and the docstring now says that explicitly. A real per-architecture artifact check would mean running the kernels, which is out of scope for this guard. Does the documented limitation cover it, or do you want the runtime check??

I ran this end to end on a **Tesla T4 (SM75)**, since that's where this crash
will hit most often once #55380 makes FlashInfer selectable on Turing again.
On Turing, FlashAttention isn't available, so FlashInfer becomes the first
candidate.

**Setup:** g4dn.2xlarge, main @ 242e4213f + this PR + #55380's SM75 floor
change, pip install (flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1, no flashinfer-cubin), ninja
on PATH, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B fp16, fresh `~/.cache/flashinfer` for each case.

| case | `is_flashinfer_jit_usable()` | selected | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| no nvcc, no jit-cache | False | TRITON_ATTN | ✅ runs |
| nvcc, no jit-cache | True | FLASHINFER | ✅ runs |
| **flashinfer-jit-cache 0.7.0.post1+cu130, no nvcc** | **True** | **FLASHINFER** | ❌ `RuntimeError: Could not find nvcc and default cuda_home='/usr/local/cuda' doesn't exist` |
| jit-cache + nvcc | True | FLASHINFER | ✅ runs |

For reference, without this PR the first case crashes with the same "Could
not find nvcc" error. So this PR fixes the plain pip install on T4.
`tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py`: 8 passed on the T4.

**The third row is a gap on SM75.** The `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel doesn't
include SM75 kernels (#55380 adds a warning about this), so on Turing
FlashInfer still JIT-compiles even when the cache is installed, and still
needs nvcc. A possible tweak:

```diff
-    if importlib.util.find_spec("flashinfer_jit_cache") is not None:
+    # flashinfer-jit-cache ships no SM75 kernels, so SM75 always needs the JIT.
+    if importlib.util.find_spec(
+        "flashinfer_jit_cache"
+    ) is not None and not current_platform.is_device_capability(75):
         return True
```

With that applied on the same T4, the third case selects TRITON_ATTN and runs,
and the jit-cache + nvcc case still selects FLASHINFER and runs. One of the new
cases in `test_flashinfer_utils.py` (jit-cache installed means usable) then
fails on an SM75 machine, so it would need the capability mocked.

Only SM75 matters here, and only after #55380, so it could also be left to
that PR. I'm happy to rerun anything on the T4.

Reading this against main `153a17166e` and FlashInfer 0.7.2, the jit-cache branch looks too loose.
Setup: this head `b18f73337b`, FlashInfer 0.7.2 with `flashinfer-jit-cache` 0.7.2+cu130 and its `sm120f` provider; source reading plus CPU probes, no GPU run.

1. **The shim alone passes.** In 0.7.2 `flashinfer-jit-cache` is a shim and the kernels come from per-arch provider packages, so `find_spec("flashinfer_jit_cache")` also passes when no provider is installed (`get_jit_cache_providers()` returns nothing).
2. **A provider alone is not enough either.** With a provider but no flashinfer-cubin or usable nvcc, and `VLLM_HAS_FLASHINFER_CUBIN=0`, `has_flashinfer()` is still False, so calling `flashinfer_xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` reaches `_missing`.

**Suggested gate:** `has_flashinfer() and ((nvcc and ninja) or compatible_provider)`. A CPU probe of the selector then chooses:

| Installed (no nvcc) | `has_flashinfer()` | Selected backend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| jit-cache shim, no provider | False | TRITON_ATTN |
| jit-cache shim plus the `sm120f` provider | False | TRITON_ATTN |
| flashinfer-cubin plus the provider | True | FLASHINFER |

The probe runs the real selector and availability functions, with package availability, backend order and other capability checks mocked.

**Why not widen `has_flashinfer()` instead:** that would also enable `concat_mla_k` for qualifying MLA dimensions, and the sm120f provider lacks its `concat_mla` module.

@waynehacking8 Thanks for catching this. I agree that the jit-cache shim can be present without any kernel provider, and that a provider alone is not enough when `has_flashinfer()` is false. I kept `has_flashinfer()` as the first check, then made the attention path require either nvcc plus ninja or a jit-cache provider with non-empty module and architecture metadata. When the active device architecture is available, the provider architecture must match it. If it cannot be read, the check falls back to non-empty provider metadata, so it cannot confirm the provider targets the active device. The exact architecture-name match may also reject compatible suffixed targets.

I added CPU cases for the shim without a provider, a provider without cubins or a usable compiler, cubins with a matching provider, and the metadata fallback. I ran the focused tests on my Mac with VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu and 13 passed. This checks provider metadata, not whether every specific kernel artifact loads.

| Device | main | this head | this head with FlashInfer's rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SM120 | FLASHINFER | TRITON_ATTN | FLASHINFER |
| SM121 | FLASHINFER | TRITON_ATTN | FLASHINFER |

So a `vllm download-kernels` install on a machine without nvcc moves from FlashInfer to Triton, which is the case the provider branch is meant to accept.

**Suggestion:** reuse FlashInfer's own rule, `select_compatible_cuda_architecture()` in `flashinfer/jit/_cuda_architecture.py` (0.7.2), or mirror it: an `a` target needs the same major and minor, while `f` and unsuffixed targets run on the same major with an equal or higher minor. FlashInfer accepts `sm120a` on SM120 as well, so the `sm120a` case at `tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py` L108-L119 would flip to accepted.

The probe, its output and the setup are in https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/0699386705fbb97ea21c5db886d2ac2b. This checks selection only; I did not run attention on a GPU.

@waynehacking8 Thanks for the probe and the gist. That exposed a real regression. I replaced the exact name match with a mirror of FlashInfer 0.7.2's compatibility rule: an `a` target needs the same major and minor, while an `f` or unsuffixed target is accepted on the same major when its minor is no newer than the device. That accepts `sm120f` on SM120 and SM121, and `sm120a` on SM120 but not SM121. I updated the SM120 `sm120a` test case accordingly. I compared the mirror against the tagged 0.7.2 source logic over 84 provider and device pairs and found no differences. On my Mac, the focused CPU tests passed: 24 passed with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. If the device architecture cannot be read, the current check falls back to non-empty provider metadata, which cannot confirm a match to the active device. Provider metadata also does not prove that every specific attention kernel artifact will load.

Rechecked a96250c273 with the same CPU selector probe: with the stock `sm120f` provider and no nvcc, SM120 and SM121 FP8 KV selection is FLASHINFER again, the same as main. Your rule also agrees with FlashInfer 0.7.2's `select_compatible_cuda_architecture()` on all 432 pairs I tried (36 provider targets against 12 unsuffixed devices), and `tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py` passes here (24 passed). The output and scripts are in the same gist, https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/0699386705fbb97ea21c5db886d2ac2b (`README-a96250c273.md`); this checks selection and unit tests only, not attention on a GPU.
